question: Why do nurses study leadership theories?

options.A: To understand leadership behavior and improve patient care
options.B: To replace clinical guidelines with administrative rules
options.C: To get automatic promotion to hospital director positions
options.D: To avoid direct bedside patient care

explanation: Leadership theories give nurses structured perspectives to analyze administrative challenges and guide staff toward better outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why must effective nurse managers know multiple leadership theories?

options.A: Single theories are illegal under international standards
options.B: Nigerian health policy mandates rotating styles monthly
options.C: Ward staff refuse managers who use only one theory
options.D: Different clinical environments and crises demand varied managerial responses

explanation: Because clinical settings vary wildly, a flexible manager draws on multiple theories to address specific situations appropriately. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the main idea behind the Great Man theory of leadership?

options.A: Leadership success depends entirely on the work environment
options.B: Effective leaders are born with traits rather than made through training
options.C: Anyone can become a great leader through university education
options.D: Followers have more power than unit managers

explanation: The Great Man theory assumes leadership is an innate quality one is born with rather than a skill learned over time. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of trait theory in modern nursing management?

options.A: It proves that experienced nurses make terrible administrative leaders
options.B: It ignores how situational factors and environmental contexts influence success
options.C: It focuses too heavily on financial budgeting instead of patient safety
options.D: It requires nurse managers to have medical degrees

explanation: Trait theory looks only at internal qualities while neglecting how changing clinical situations affect a leader's performance. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which leadership style involves the manager making all decisions without staff input?
explanation: An autocratic leader retains total control and makes decisions independently without consulting subordinates. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h3)

question: A nurse manager faces a sudden mass casualty arrival. Which leadership style is best for this moment?
explanation: Rapid crises require quick, direct commands without lengthy group discussions, making an autocratic style effective in emergencies. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h3)

question: According to situational leadership, how should a manager guide inexperienced nursing students?

options.A: Adopt a laissez-faire approach to encourage independent thinking
options.B: Focus exclusively on paperwork rather than clinical oversight
options.C: Punish minor mistakes immediately to deter poor habits
options.D: Provide high task direction and close supervision until competence grows

explanation: Inexperienced staff require structured guidance and close supervision until their readiness and skill levels improve. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the core premise of contingency and situational leadership theories?

options.A: A single fixed leadership style works equally well in all departments
options.B: The best leadership style changes based on the situation and follower readiness
options.C: Patient outcomes depend solely on hospital funding
options.D: Only senior nurses with master's degrees possess true leadership capability

explanation: Situational theories dictate that effective leaders adapt their behavior to fit the demands of the current context and staff maturity. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h4)

question: What primary mechanism does a transactional leader use to motivate staff?

options.A: A system of rewards and corrective disciplinary actions
options.B: Focusing entirely on personal spiritual growth and humility
options.C: Inspiring a shared vision of future healthcare transformation
options.D: Allowing staff complete freedom without any rules or oversight

explanation: Transactional leadership relies on contractual exchanges, rewarding compliance and correcting non-compliance. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is transactional leadership insufficient on its own for long-term unit development?

options.A: It forces nurse managers to perform bedside nursing duties
options.B: It eliminates all forms of accountability and performance appraisal
options.C: It maintains daily operations but fails to inspire innovation or deep emotional commitment
options.D: It is strictly illegal under Nigerian nursing council regulations

explanation: While transactional methods keep the ward running, they rely on compliance rather than inspiring genuine passion or creativity in staff. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h5)

question: How does transformational leadership differ fundamentally from transactional leadership?

options.A: It requires the leader to remain completely uninvolved in daily ward routines
options.B: It focuses exclusively on punishment for clinical errors rather than mentoring
options.C: It inspires emotional commitment and shared vision rather than relying solely on rewards and rules
options.D: It applies only to physicians and doctors rather than nursing personnel

explanation: Transformational leaders elevate staff aspirations and engagement, moving beyond simple contractual compliance. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h6)

question: A nurse manager wants to overhaul an outdated triage system. Which action reflects transformational leadership?

options.A: Articulating a compelling vision of improved patient safety and mentoring staff through change
options.B: Offering a cash bonus solely for paperwork without staff discussion
options.C: Threatening queries for anyone who questions hospital protocol
options.D: Ignoring the problem and letting nurses figure out a new system

explanation: Transformational leaders engage, inspire, and mentor their teams to embrace meaningful clinical improvements. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of a servant leader in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Prioritizing the growth, well-being, and support of the nursing staff
options.B: Maximizing hospital revenue generation through aggressive cost-cutting
options.C: Ensuring the manager receives personal recognition for ward achievements
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital hierarchy and maintaining rigid control

explanation: Servant leadership flips traditional hierarchy by placing the leader in a position to support and uplift subordinates first. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is authentic leadership crucial for encouraging incident reporting among junior nurses?

options.A: Transparent and self-aware leaders build psychological safety so staff report errors without fear
options.B: Authentic leaders possess medical degrees that prevent clinical mistakes
options.C: Staff are legally required to obey authentic managers without asking questions
options.D: It legally exempts nurses from facing disciplinary panels after major drug errors

explanation: Authenticity and transparency create a safe environment where nurses can report near-misses honestly to improve systems. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h7)

question: A Nigerian ward manager faces severe nurse shortages and power outages. Which approach best addresses staff burnout?

options.A: Using transactional discipline as the sole method to force compliance
options.B: Relying strictly on autocratic punishments for nurses who feel overwhelmed
options.C: Adopting a pure laissez-faire approach and ignoring operational challenges
options.D: Combining transformational support with situational flexibility and genuine staff advocacy

explanation: Navigating tough systemic challenges requires adaptive, supportive leadership that empowers staff and advocates for their well-being. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h8)

question: What is a major risk of relying solely on rigid autocratic management in Nigerian public hospitals experiencing brain drain?

options.A: It increases staff frustration and accelerates the migration of nurses abroad
options.B: It forces hospital management to increase salaries across all departments
options.C: It eliminates all forms of inter-professional conflict
options.D: It automatically solves all infrastructural and drug supply shortages

explanation: Harsh, unsupportive management under difficult working conditions drives frustrated nurses to seek employment abroad. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h8)
